sources.title: WHO Guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
CDC Physical Activity Guidelines for School-Aged Children and Adolescents
AAP Resistance Training for Children and Adolescents

hardStops.message: Stop the session and tell a parent, guardian, coach, or another responsible adult. Seek advice from a qualified healthcare professional when appropriate.

readinessRules.message: Choose an easy recovery session or rest instead of adding a performance session.

matchRules.message: Keep activity easy close to a match and preserve energy for the fixed team commitment.

recentLoadRules.message: Avoid stacking another performance session within 24 hours of a high-load activity.

weeklyRules.message: The app should complement team football, school activity, rest, and free play rather than maximize extra sessions.

supervisionRules.message: Strength, speed, and change-of-direction sessions require qualified adult supervision and technique feedback.

progressionRules.message: Progress repetitions, duration, complexity, or resistance one at a time after consistently controlled sessions.

requiredMessages.general: These sessions are general training guidance for healthy youth footballers and are not medical care.
requiredMessages.guardian: A parent or guardian must approve participation and know when and where the session is taking place.
requiredMessages.stop: Stop immediately if pain, dizziness, faintness, chest discomfort, unusual breathing difficulty, or feeling unwell occurs.
requiredMessages.supervision: Use the supervision level shown for the routine. Technique quality matters more than repetitions, speed, or resistance.
